title: Hospital System Schema Design
description: Model patients, doctors, appointments, prescriptions, and medical records

data.text: Hospital schemas must track patients, staff, appointments, diagnoses, prescriptions, and billing. Data integrity and audit trails are critical for compliance and care coordination.

data.title: Hospital DDL
data.content: Design core tables for patients, doctors, appointments, and medical records.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE patients (
  patient_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  date_of_birth DATE NOT NULL,
  gender CHAR(1),
  phone VARCHAR(32),
  insurance_id VARCHAR(64)
);

CREATE TABLE doctors (
  doctor_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  specialty VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(32)
);

CREATE TABLE appointments (
  appointment_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  patient_id INT NOT NULL,
  doctor_id INT NOT NULL,
  appointment_date DATE NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled'
);

CREATE TABLE medical_records (
  record_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
  patient_id INT NOT NULL,
  doctor_id INT NOT NULL,
  diagnosis TEXT,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

data.title: Warning
data.text: Medical records require strict access controls and audit logging. Plan encryption and row-level security from the start.

items.question: How do I handle patient allergies across visits?
items.answer: Create a patient_allergies table for many-to-many allergy tracking with severity and reaction details.

items.question: Should appointments store time ranges?
items.answer: Yes. Use start_time and end_time DATETIME columns and add a unique constraint to prevent double-booking doctors.

items.question: How do I link prescriptions to diagnoses?
items.answer: Use a prescriptions table with diagnosis_id foreign key and medication details.

data.title: Summary
points: Use patient_id and doctor_id as central keys
Track appointment status for scheduling logic
Plan access control and audit from day one
data.takeaway: Hospital schemas prioritize data integrity, auditability, and compliance while supporting clinical workflows.
